name: Djembe
shortDescription: West African goblet drum with rope-tensioned goatskin membrane producing bass, tone, and slap timbres.
description: The djembe is a goblet-shaped drum carved from a single hardwood log and covered with a shaved goatskin membrane tensioned by vertical ropes and metal rings. Three distinct timbres emerge depending on where and how the hand strikes the head: the bass (centre strike, flat hand) produces a low fundamental; the tone (edge strike, fingers together) produces a clear mid-frequency; the slap (edge strike, cupped fingers released) produces a sharp high-frequency crack.
historicalOrigins: Originated with the Mandé people of West Africa (modern Mali/Guinea), used in ceremony and communication. Djembe means 'everyone gather together in peace' in the Bambara language.
acousticPrinciples: Circular membrane: strike position determines which Bessel mode is excited (J₀ = bass; J₁ = tone)
Goblet shell acts as Helmholtz resonator boosting bass fundamental through the open bottom port
Goatskin membrane tension determines fundamental pitch; higher tension = higher pitch
Bass tones open the shell resonance port; slaps close it momentarily to produce the crack

characteristics.pitchRange: Bass: 60–120 Hz; Tone: 200–400 Hz; Slap: 500 Hz – 3 kHz
characteristics.timbralColor: Rich bass, clear tone, crisp slap — all from the same instrument
characteristics.orchestralRole: Ensemble rhythm leader (Sangban/Dunun pairing), ceremonial, solo

soundDNA.exciter: Hand striking goatskin membrane — flat, cupped finger, or slap technique
soundDNA.resonator: Carved hardwood goblet shell with open bottom port
soundDNA.harmonics: Bessel inharmonic modes; bass centre strike dominant fundamental
soundDNA.timbreProfile: Warm deep bass, clear cutting tone, explosive slap crack
soundDNA.radiationPattern: Top radiation from membrane; bass port radiates downward/omnidirectional

membrane.label: Goatskin Membrane (Batter Head)
membrane.function: Shaved goatskin membrane vibrating in Bessel mode patterns when struck.

characteristics.mechanism: Circular membrane Bessel mode vibration J₀/J₁

shell.label: Carved Hardwood Shell
shell.function: Goblet-shaped shell couples membrane vibration to internal air column and open port.

characteristics.material: Carved lenké, iroko, or plantation mahogany
characteristics.mechanism: Helmholtz resonator with open bottom port

tension_ropes.label: Tension Rope System
tension_ropes.function: Vertical ropes threaded between top and bottom rings adjust membrane tension and pitch.

characteristics.material: Braided nylon or polyester rope, galvanised iron rings
characteristics.mechanism: Rope tension increases membrane T (raises pitch)

crown_ring.label: Crown Ring
crown_ring.function: Upper iron ring holding membrane skin folded over the drum top.

followTheSound.title: Hand Strike
followTheSound.explanation: Hand technique determines Bessel mode: centre (J₀ bass), edge (J₁ tone), slap (J₁ + noise).

followTheSound.title: Membrane Tension
followTheSound.explanation: Rope tension controls membrane T; tighter ropes raise pitch across all timbres.

followTheSound.title: Goblet Resonance
followTheSound.explanation: Shell Helmholtz resonator boosts bass fundamental and colours tone through shell reflection.

followTheSound.title: Air Port Radiation
followTheSound.explanation: Open bottom port radiates bass downward; total sound projects from both membrane and port.
